[b]October 15, 2027: The National Redeployment Act[/b]

Following a push by the SCSID in the grand assembly, the National Redeployment Act of 2027 has finally passed after six months of legislative gridlock over what exactly would be done with 1.45 Million soldiers and 500,000 reservists who were to be cut under the SCSID efficiency model.

Ultimately the bill would move to form a special department for Veteran Relocation which would move to aide the laid off soldiers into a transitory period, connecting them with the necessary resources to gain new jobs and ensure a consistent and reliable income was maintained.

The bill furthermore would move to gradually phase the soldiers out with an estimated plan for 3 phaseouts to be completed by 2029 with 483,000 soldiers being laid off once a year to prevent flooding the market with unemployed soldiers.

[b]October 19, 2027: A Unified Doctrine on Rosenmarkket-Shamatine Relations[/b]

Whereas relations between the world and the nations of Shamat have been rife with the question of colonialism and opposition against the various groups and states that populate the Shamatine continents, there has arisen a resilient motion forward by the nations of Shamat to push back against these questions and attitudes by adopting a post-colonial view of Shamat through the notions of Pan-Shamatism. 

As a result, the nations of the world, unsure of what exactly to do with this push by the native states towards unity, have no comprehensive diplomatic or military strategy beyond the basic nation-to-nation bilateral frameworks that have dominated the international relations scene since the rise of the modern era. 

However, as Shamat moves towards a post-colonial order, the necessity of a unified geopolitical doctrine and military template has become far clearer. 

It is thus that the government of Rosenmarkke, under the initiative of the D-29 doctrine, has moved to formulate the following doctrine for Rosenmarkke-Shamat relations.

[list]
A. Economic interconnection is a key strategy to a unified post-colonial Shamatine state, whereas Rosenmarkke should pursue a single economic treaty template with all nations on Shamat.

B. Military standardisation and cooperation across all major Shamatine states provides for a stronger Shamat, and as such, Rosenmarkke should utilise a standardised military framework consisting of procurement, training, and intelligence sharing.

C. Cultural differences are notably present in Shamatine states, whereas a single cultural framework should not (and cannot) be utilised in the formation of relations with Shamatine states. 
[/list]

Under these guidelines, Rosenmarkke may advance the cause of a unified Shamat under the terms and guidelines of the Shamatine Security Pact, through a strategic unified partnership model.

[b][u]A Summit For The Economic Future Of Shamat[/u][/b]

President Fereydun Khan reads over the prepared letter from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs at dawn.

"This is good. Is everything else prepared?"

"Yes, we have a venue and security ready."

"Send it out to our partners. God willing everything will go well."

Jalayer Khan, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, smirks. "You've been reading too much of Irocco's and Baladullah's news."

"What can I say, it's an easy phrase," President Khan says with a grin. "Enough of this, send the message out to our partners. [I]God willing[/i] we'll lead Shamat towards unity."

-----

In the next few hours, the invitations are sent to each nation's respective Ministries of Foreign Affairs:

[I]"[b]Invitation to The First Shamat Economic Community Summit[/b]

On behalf of the Government of President Fereydun Khan of Dhornaper, we extend a formal invitation to your government to attend the first summit for the Shamat Economic Community, to be held in our capital Shar.

The summit will bring together multiple Shamatine states committed to cooperation and the shared responsibility of establishing a common economic base for mutual prosperity.

Our agenda proposes the Shamat Economic Community previously presented to your governments with the aim of strengthening Shanat's economic resilience and independence, coordinating economic policy of key resources for mutual benefit, and establishing economic security for member states to resist the scourge of colonialism.

Your delegations will receive the necessary details as attached in this message. As the host, we will guarantee that we will only proceed with the Shamat Economic Community when every participant is prepared and willing to join.

We look forward to welcoming your representatives to Shar.

Signed,  

Jalayer Khan, Minister of Foreign Affairs"[/i]
